Iron oxide isn't just one color. It can be a range of colors from yellow, orange, red, brown or black. Our blood does not contain raw iron oxide. The iron is part of the hemoglobin and the overall molecule has a particular wavelength absorption signature. As the graph shows, hemoglobin absorbs most visible light wavelengths outside of the red portion of the spectrum. This makes it red. The different curves show the shift in the absorption when hemoglobin is carrying oxygen versus carbon dioxide. It's not a large shift and the blood stays very much on the red reflecting side of things.

TL;DR - Blood is red because hemoglobin absorbs most wavelengths of visible light outside of the red wavelengths.
